name: Pour latte art
description: Steam milk to optimal temperature and texture, then execute a precise pour to create a crisp rosetta latte art design. Key learned target values are heating milk to 65 °C (or between 58.4 °C and 65 °C), starting the pour at a height of 9 cm, and dropping in to draw the design at 50.3% cup fill.

learned_parameters.label: Heat the milk
learned_parameters.rationale: Target 65 °C yields a perfect 100/100 sub-score (as demonstrated in Attempt #2: 65 °C -> 100, Attempt #4: 65 °C -> 100, Attempt #6: 58.4 °C -> 100, Attempt #9: 65 °C -> 100, and Attempt #10: 65 °C -> 100). Lower temperatures like 50 °C produced flat, lukewarm milk with poor foam (Attempt #1: 50 °C -> sub-score 38). Overheating to 74 °C resulted in scalded milk and stiff foam (Attempt #5: 74 °C -> sub-score 20). Supported by Verve Coffee guidelines recommending steaming milk between 135-150 °F (57-65 °C). Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 65 °C. Tried 50 °C (sub-score 38) to 74 °C (sub-score 20). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 58.4 °C and 65 °C. Too high (74 °C): "Scalded milk: cooked taste, sweetness gone, foam dry and stiff."

learned_parameters.label: Pour height
learned_parameters.rationale: Target 9 cm achieves a perfect 100/100 sub-score (Attempt #4: 9 cm -> 100, Attempt #6: 9 cm -> 100, Attempt #9: 9 cm -> 100, Attempt #10: 9 cm -> 100). Pouring too low at 4.8 cm or 6.6 cm spreads foam over the crema prematurely (Attempt #3: 4.8 cm -> sub-score 28; Attempt #8: 6.6 cm -> sub-score 78). Pouring too high at 11.4 cm or 12 cm splashes and breaks the crema (Attempt #1: 12 cm -> sub-score 61; Attempt #7: 11.4 cm -> sub-score 78). Attempt #2 at 7 cm scored 88. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 9 cm. Tried 4.8 cm (sub-score 28) to 12 cm (sub-score 61). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 7 cm and 9 cm. Too high (11.4 cm): "Poured from too high: the stream splashed and broke up the crema." Too low (6.6 cm): "Poured too close too early: white foam spread over the crema, no canvas left."

learned_parameters.label: When to drop in
learned_parameters.rationale: Target 50.3% fill yields a perfect 100/100 sub-score across all attempts tested (Attempts #2, #3, #4, #5, #6, #7, #8, #9, #10: 50.3% -> sub-score 100). In contrast, waiting until 65% fill leaves insufficient room for the leaves to develop (Attempt #1: 65% -> sub-score 46, feedback 'Dropped in too late'). Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 50.3 % full. Tried 50.3 % full (sub-score 100) to 65 % full (sub-score 46). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 50.3 % full and 50.3 % full.

control_effects.effect: Controls milk sweetness and foam texture. Scored 100 at 65 °C (Attempts #2, #4, #7-#10) and 58.4 °C (Attempt #6). Scored 38 at 50 °C due to lukewarm flat foam (Attempt #1), and plummeted to 20 at 74 °C due to scalded, cooked taste and dry foam (Attempt #5). Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 65 °C. Tried 50 °C (sub-score 38) to 74 °C (sub-score 20). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 58.4 °C and 65 °C. Too high (74 °C): "Scalded milk: cooked taste, sweetness gone, foam dry and stiff."

Governs whether milk sinks beneath crema or washes it out. Peaked at 100 at 9 cm (Attempts #4, #6, #9, #10). Sub-scores degraded symmetrically when departing from 9 cm: 7.0 cm scored 88 (Attempt #2), 6.6 cm and 11.4 cm both scored 78 (Attempts #8, #7), 12.0 cm scored 61 (Attempt #1), and 4.8 cm scored 28 (Attempt #3). Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 9 cm. Tried 4.8 cm (sub-score 28) to 12 cm (sub-score 61). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 7 cm and 9 cm. Too high (11.4 cm): "Poured from too high: the stream splashed and broke up the crema." Too low (6.6 cm): "Poured too close too early: white foam spread over the crema, no canvas left."

Determines the available canvas for latte art. Scored 100 at 50.3% (Attempts #2-#10). Dropped to 46 at 65% with feedback warning that drop-in was too late and cramped the rosetta (Attempt #1). Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 50.3 % full. Tried 50.3 % full (sub-score 100) to 65 % full (sub-score 46). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 50.3 % full and 50.3 % full.

steps: Steam the milk to a target temperature of 65 °C (or within the acceptable sweet spot of 58.4 °C to 65 °C) to ensure a sweet, glossy microfoam without scalding.
Begin integrating the milk into the espresso base from an initial pour height of 9 cm to dive under the crema without splashing or washing it out.
When the cup reaches 50.3% fill, lower the pitcher tip close to the surface ('drop in') and initiate the side-to-side wiggle to draw the rosetta leaf pattern before finishing with a pull-through.
caveats: Qualitative feedback takes priority: if the stream splashes crema or foam prematurely covers the surface, height and timing must be adjusted rather than relying on unguided sweeps.
Do not drop in too late; waiting past the halfway mark (e.g., at 65% fill) cramps the design and leaves no canvas.
Steaming past 70 °C risks ruining milk sweetness and texture; keep temperature well under 74 °C.
Maintain steady pitcher control; both dropping too low too early (<7 cm) and pouring too high (>11 cm) significantly drop the pour height sub-score.
Systematic search suggestion advised probing higher on height and fill percentage, but qualitative feedback explicitly says poured too high and dropped in too late; feedback must take precedence.

problems.problem: Lukewarm milk: flat, barely sweet, and the foam never turned glossy.
problems.fix: Increase milk steaming temperature to 65 °C (hold steaming longer until reaching 58.4 °C–65 °C).

problems.problem: Dropped in too late: no room left, the rosetta came out cramped and tiny.
problems.fix: Drop the pitcher close to the surface earlier, right when the cup reaches approximately 50.3% capacity.

problems.problem: Poured from too high: the stream splashed and broke up the crema.
problems.fix: Lower the initial pour height to 9 cm to prevent the stream from disrupting the espresso crema.

problems.problem: Pour height at 7.0 cm was still slightly off optimal (scored 88/100).
Poured too close too early: white foam spread over the crema, no canvas left.
problems.fix: Raise the initial pour height to 9 cm and maintain it during the mixing phase so the milk dives under the crema.
